passage: Atoms are the fundamental building blocks of all matter, yet they are mostly empty space rather than solid spheres. When atoms combine to form molecules, they do so in fixed, definite proportions by mass, regardless of the source or method of preparation of the substance. For instance, water molecules always contain hydrogen and oxygen in a constant ratio, whether obtained from a river or a laboratory. During chemical reactions, the total mass of the reactants remains equal to the total mass of the products, even if a gas is released, provided the reaction occurs in a closed system. To quantify these substances, we use the mole concept. One mole of any substance contains 6.022 x 10^23 particles, and its mass in grams is numerically equal to its molar mass. Importantly, molar mass represents the mass of one mole of particles, not the mass of a single atom or molecule. Furthermore, ions are formed when atoms lose or gain electrons, not protons, to achieve stability. Understanding these principles allows us to predict how matter behaves and transforms during various chemical processes.

items.evidence: For instance, water molecules always contain hydrogen and oxygen in a constant ratio, whether obtained from a river or a laboratory.
items.q: Water is made in a lab by a new method. How will its hydrogen-oxygen ratio compare?
options: It will be the same as river water
It will differ with the new method
It will change with the lab's heat
It will favour whichever gas was added first
items.explain: Water has a constant ratio of hydrogen and oxygen, whatever its source or method of preparation.

wrong.why: thinks the ratio depends on how it was prepared
links heat to changes in matter
thinks the first ingredient decides the ratio

items.evidence: During chemical reactions, the total mass of the reactants remains equal to the total mass of the products, even if a gas is released, provided the reaction occurs in a closed system.
items.q: A reaction in a sealed flask makes a gas. Why does the flask's total mass stay the same?
options: The gas stays inside, so no mass escapes
The gas has no mass, so nothing changes
Mass is lost but the glass gains it back
The products weigh less than the reactants
items.explain: In a closed system, products have the same total mass as reactants, even when a gas forms.

wrong.why: thinks gases weigh nothing so mass is lost
makes up a transfer of mass to the container
thinks mass drops when a gas is produced

items.evidence: Importantly, molar mass represents the mass of one mole of particles, not the mass of a single atom or molecule.
items.q: A student says molar mass of a substance is the mass of one molecule. What is wrong?
options: It is the mass of a whole mole of particles
It is the mass of one atom in grams
It is the mass of 6.022 particles only
It is the mass of one ion of the substance
items.explain: Molar mass is the mass of one mole of particles, not of a single atom or molecule.

wrong.why: thinks it is the mass of a single atom
misreads 6.022 x 10^23 as a small number
mixes mass with ionic charge ideas

items.evidence: Furthermore, ions are formed when atoms lose or gain electrons, not protons, to achieve stability.
items.q: How does a neutral atom turn into a positive ion?
options: It loses one or more electrons
It gains one or more protons
It gains one or more electrons
It loses one or more protons
items.explain: Ions form when atoms lose or gain electrons, not protons; losing electrons leaves a positive charge.

wrong.why: thinks a cation forms by gaining protons
reverses which electron change gives positive charge
thinks protons are lost instead of electrons
